Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-12 10:00 AM PT
- Duration: 42 minutes

- Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Marketing), Jamie Roberts (Brightwave), Taylor Nguyen (Brightwave), Luis Ortega (Brightwave Eng)

Auto-summary: Quick 30-40 minute customer spotlight interview. Focus on Brightwave's product use of Redwood for content generation and personalization; mentioned Dedicated/reserved capacity and VPC for PII-safe experiments; ROI discussion (token cost reduction via caching and batching), quick anecdote about a migration hiccup and how Redwood's SE helped.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Alex from Redwood Marketing, I'm here with Priya and Samir, and of course Jamie, Taylor and Luis from Brightwave. How we doing?
[00:05] Jamie Roberts: Hey Alex, good morning, excited to be on. Thanks for having us.
[00:07] Taylor Nguyen: Morning, yeah this is fun.
[00:12] Alex Morgan: Cool. Quick note, we're recording for about 30 to 40 minutes, we'll pull some clips for social, and we'll send the transcript for approvals. Sound good?
[00:18] Jamie Roberts: Yep sounds good.

[00:30] Alex Morgan: So to kick off, can you give our listeners a quick background on Brightwave and how you're using Redwood?
[00:34] Jamie Roberts: Sure. So Brightwave is a digital health content platform, we do personalized patient education and care navigation. We started using Redwood late 2024 for real-time content generation — things like tailored appointment summaries and conversational triage flows. The goal was to be faster than our old setup and cheaper than running everything in-house.
[00:55] Alex Morgan: Nice, and what was your stack before Redwood?
[00:59] Luis Ortega: We were running a mix of in-house inference on older GPUs and a managed endpoint from another cloud vendor. It was fine for batch jobs but latency was inconsistent for interactive flows, and cost was spiking when we had bursts.
[01:15] Priya Desai: When you evaluated Redwood what were the key criteria you were looking at?
[01:20] Jamie Roberts: Primarily latency and predictable cost, plus security controls — we deal with PHI so things like VPC, KMS and audit logs were must-haves. Also the ability to measure quality regressions because our clinicians need output to be stable.
[01:36] Taylor Nguyen: And the developer DX — we wanted an API that our front-end teams could call without complicated ops work.

[01:50] Alex Morgan: Great. Can you walk through the migration — any surprises?
[01:54] Luis Ortega: Migration was relatively smooth but there was one hiccup: we tried to lift-and-shift a quantized model variant and saw garbled tokenization in some clinical prompts — turned out to be a mismatch in tokenizer version. Priya and her team helped debug; we ended up pinning a specific model version and the Redwood runtime's kernel selection handled the rest.
[02:20] Priya Desai: Yeah I remember that. We recommended a small test harness and a canary rollout, kept KV cache warm for the most common prefixes, that dropped p99 latency by like 150ms for the triage flow.

[02:40] Alex Morgan: Jamie, can you quantify the benefits? Latency, cost, anything else?
[02:45] Jamie Roberts: Sure. For our interactive triage flow p50 latency went from roughly 480ms to about 220ms after we moved to Redwood Dedicated with the right batching config. Cost per 1k tokens dropped ~28% thanks to improved batching, prefix caching and switching to a quantized variant for non-sensitive calls. The real win was predictability — reserved capacity meant we didn't hit surprise overages during campaigns.
[03:10] Samir Patel: That's an awesome stat — and the predictability part is huge for procurement.

[03:20] Alex Morgan: Let's talk about security — you mentioned PHI. Did you use Redwood Private or VPC options?
[03:27] Jamie Roberts: We initially used Redwood Hosted in a dedicated tenancy, then moved to a VPC Private deployment for our production PHI flows. We wanted the control for KMS integration and to have audit logs forwarded to Splunk. The transition required some networking tweaks but Redwood's private deploy checklist was really helpful.
[03:48] Taylor Nguyen: And SSO integration with our Okta was seamless, which helped with RBAC for the content team.

[04:05] Alex Morgan: Nice. Any pushback or concerns from stakeholders?
[04:09] Jamie Roberts: Procurement asked about vendor lock-in and model portability. We ran a short proof comparing Redwood's hosted model variants vs a self-hosted model and the difference in ops cost made the decision clearer — we didn't want to own the full stack.
[04:25] Luis Ortega: On engineering side we wanted some determinism around KV cache behavior — Redwood's docs and the SE-run performance workshop made that easier to plan.

[04:40] Alex Morgan: Quick aside — anyone mention competitors in your RFP?
[04:43] Jamie Roberts: Yeah briefly OpenAI and a couple of managed cloud vendors — main question was about SLA and private deployment options.

[04:55] Alex Morgan: For future features or improvements what would you like to see?
[04:59] Taylor Nguyen: Better out-of-the-box eval tooling for clinical prompts — like a curated prompt-set runner and automated regression alerts.
[05:07] Jamie Roberts: Also tighter billing attribution per route would help with product-level chargeback.

[05:20] Alex Morgan: Great feedback, we'll capture that. Any quick customer anecdotes to share?
[05:24] Jamie Roberts: One that stands out — during a regional vaccination drive we had a sudden surge. Because we were on Reserved Dedicated capacity with autoscale burst we kept triage and scheduling flows online; our customer support tickets actually dropped because the bot handled early intake better. That was a big win for execs.
[05:45] Samir Patel: Love that. We'll ask to include that in the written case study.

[06:00] Alex Morgan: Alright, last few minutes — recap and next steps. Priya?
[06:05] Priya Desai: We'll produce an edit of the audio and a short 45-60s clip for socials. I'll share the performance workshop deck and the canary rollout checklist.
[06:16] Samir Patel: I'll follow up on a draft case study and the quote approvals. Jamie, you'll approve the transcript and the quotes by next week?
[06:24] Jamie Roberts: Yep I can do that by 2026-03-16.
[06:28] Alex Morgan: Awesome. Any last bits?
[06:30] Taylor Nguyen: No, thanks all.
[06:32] Luis Ortega: Thanks, great to talk.
[06:35] Alex Morgan: Thanks everyone, we'll send the files. End recording.
